title: Bumrah to Skip New Zealand ODIs, Build for Tests via India A Match
excerpt: Fully fit but carefully managed, India's pace leader will play one red-ball India A game from November 6 before the Wellington Test on November 19.
body:
• Jasprit Bumrah is unlikely to play India's five ODIs in New Zealand; team management wants him fresh for the two Tests, with the first Test starting in Wellington on November 19.
  • Bumrah is fully fit and has begun red-ball preparation in Ahmedabad; the plan is one India A match, starting around November 6, to build his workload before the Tests.
  • A knee injury kept him out of the Sri Lanka Tests earlier this year, and his last multi-day match was against South Africa at home last year.
  • The same protective approach is expected before next year's five-Test Australia series, with the World Test Championship the stated priority.

India's team management has settled on a protective plan for Jasprit Bumrah on the New Zealand tour: skip the five-match ODI series, build red-ball workload in one India A fixture, and arrive fresh for the Tests. Bumrah is completely fit, according to The Times of India, but the think-tank wants him focused on the red-ball leg rather than switching formats mid-tour.

The Plan in Detail

Bumrah has already started red-ball preparations in Ahmedabad and is expected at the BCCI Centre of Excellence later this month before flying to New Zealand. The workload step is the third India A fixture, which begins on November 6, leaving a workable gap before the first Test in Wellington on November 19. Sportskeeda, reporting the same plan, noted the India A red-ball series runs from October 24 and that Bumrah was also left out of the T20I squad for the tour. He was not part of the home ODI and T20I squads against West Indies either, and last played in India's Asian Games campaign in Japan.

"Bumrah is completely fit, but for a long tour, it's important to prioritise. The Test series is very important."

— Source tracking developments, quoted by The Times of India

Why India Is Being Careful

The caution has a recent history. A knee injury ruled Bumrah out of the two Tests against Sri Lanka earlier this year, and his last multi-day fixture was against South Africa at home last year. Sportskeeda added that his last red-ball appearance came in the second Test against South Africa in Guwahati in November 2025. India, led by Shubman Gill, sit fifth in the World Test Championship standings, which makes the New Zealand Tests more valuable to the team than bilateral ODIs with no championship points attached. The source quoted by TOI put the logic bluntly: there is no point making the leader of the bowling pack slog through ODIs and then suddenly shift focus to red-ball cricket.

Beyond New Zealand

The thinking extends past this tour. Multiple discussions have covered not only New Zealand but also the five Tests against Australia early next year, and a similar approach is expected in the build-up to that series, keeping Bumrah away from what the source called inconsequential bilaterals. That is a notable shift in how India handles its most valuable fast bowler: fewer white-ball appearances by default, with selection driven by the Test calendar.

India's ODI and Test squads are expected in the next few days, with selectors still waiting on updates for Harshit Rana, Prasidh Krishna and Rishabh Pant. For diaspora fans planning around the tour, the practical takeaway is simple: expect Bumrah in whites in Wellington from November 19, and do not count on seeing him in the ODI leg. His India A outing in early November will be the first real sighting of his Test readiness.
